content:
#39110 fixes the first places that would break if Set α wasn't defeq to α → Prop.
#39211 is a big PR by @Yury G. Kudryashov to fix all of it.

@Yury G. Kudryashov What's your plan with the big PR? Are you looking for help, and/or for splicing things from the big PR, or are you attempting to fix everything in one PR? What are your thoughts on #39110? (and of my previous #39099 and #39147)

cc @Monica Omar @Anne Baanen

Also we haven't decided on a name for the Set α ≃ α → Prop equivalence yet :sweat_smile:
Set.toProp / Set.toPredicate / setEquivPredicate / Set.equivPredicate / Equiv.setPredicate / Equiv.setOf / setOfEquiv / ...
Oh right, for the name I think either Set.toProp or Set.toPredicate would be good. I don't really have a strong opinion on either
It would be good to rename docs#setOf to Set.of. Then (α → Prop) ≃ Set α can be Set.ofEquiv.
That's a good name too
I like that idea, but it sounds like a huge diff, renamed to Set.toProp for now
@Snir Broshi My plan was to start with fixes that don't require changes near the definition of Set.
There are a few files, where defeq abuse is important for API, and I think that they should be refactored first.
I'll post details tomorrow.

In my big PR, I use

structure Set (\a : Type*) where
  Mem : \a -> Prop
There is also a large refactor about defeq abuse for EventuallyEq/EventuallyLE for sets. I'm going to cherry-pick the relevant parts, add deprecations, and open a PR, probably tomorrow.
Okay, but can you explain why this PR can't be merged? It was previously delegated

It creates unnecessary merge conflicts with large PR without resolving any defeq abuses that aren't resolved there. I'm flying today, so I can't have a better look until tomorrow. It's possible that you made better decisions and we should merge it, I'll tell you my opinion tomorrow.

If you want to fix one of the few leaf nodes that abuse defeq in essential way, then https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Combinatorics/Hindman.html is a good candidate. IMHO, we should deprecate ad-hoc definitions and use Finsets of Finsupps instead.
Also, we should use Nat -> M instead of Stream's.
This way the file will maintain interoperability with other parts of the library.
Currently, the file uses FS both as a predicate and as a set.
Hey, any updates?
Sorry, I'll have a look tomorrow. I'm busy with moving, and forgot about it. Thanks for the reminder!

Yaël Dillies said:

It would be good to rename docs#setOf to Set.of. Then (α → Prop) ≃ Set α can be Set.ofEquiv.

How about having the equivalence (α → Prop) ≃ Set α be Set.of and then we'll later deprecate docs#setOf (that's what we have for matrices: docs#Matrix.of is an equivalence)?

I much prefer the constructor to get the shorter name and the equiv to be suffixed with Equiv. It makes the naming more consistent with further bundlings of the constructor, eg we could have Set.ofOrderIso too
To me, Set.ofOrderIso reads like it's trying to build a set from an order iso, which is a similar reading to docs#OrderDual.ofDual docs#Additive.ofMul docs#WithTop.ofDual etc.
I agree. That's why I would prefer to rename setOf to Set.ofPred (but it's a bigger change naming-wise)
